overall.wands.11.reversed.pause: Don't recommend an opportunity to others while the details are still unconfirmed. If you agree to join together and the details change, they could be caught off guard too.

overall.wands.12.upright.headline: Taking action yourself could bring quick progress.
paragraphs: Getting out and doing something could be rewarding today. A visit you've put off or a new activity may go better than expected, and you could settle in quickly somewhere unfamiliar and enjoy the experience. Trying something you've spent a long time considering may make the answer clearer.
If there's somewhere you've wanted to visit, check when you can go and make the trip. Planning too many stops in your excitement could leave you little time to enjoy them.
overall.wands.12.upright.do: If there's somewhere you've wanted to visit, find out when you can go and make the trip.
overall.wands.12.upright.pause: Don't plan too many stops in one day just because you're excited. Rushing to the next place could leave you less time to stay and enjoy where you are.

overall.wands.12.reversed.headline: A sudden change of mind could interrupt your plans.
paragraphs: Something you start may be difficult to see through today. Someone who agreed to join you could drop out, or a hastily arranged visit may be cancelled, leaving you with a wasted trip. Arranging something else on the spot to make up for it could go wrong again.
Before setting off, check that things are still going ahead. If you can no longer go yourself, let the other person know straight away.
overall.wands.12.reversed.do: If you've arranged to meet someone or visit them, check with them before setting off that it's still going ahead.
overall.wands.12.reversed.pause: Don't rush to make another arrangement just because one was cancelled. Checking that the other person is available before deciding can reduce the chance of changing the new plan too.

overall.wands.13.upright.headline: People could respond warmly and make the day enjoyable.
paragraphs: You may find a welcoming face wherever you go today. Something you bring up could draw interest, and an invitation to do something together is likely to receive a good response. You may have a chance to show what you do well without having to force it.
If there's something you'd like to say to a group, feel free to bring it up. Give others time to join in too, so everyone can enjoy the conversation.
overall.wands.13.upright.do: If there's something you'd like to share while spending time with a group, feel free to bring it up first.
overall.wands.13.upright.pause: Don't keep talking only about yourself because people are responding well. Pausing to let others join in can make the conversation more enjoyable.

overall.wands.13.reversed.headline: Worrying about people's reactions could make things uncomfortable.
paragraphs: People may be less receptive to what you want than usual today. Someone else getting more attention could hurt your feelings, or a quiet response may make your tone sharper. Trying too hard to gain recognition could leave people even less interested.
After speaking, give the other person time to share their thoughts too. Pointing out faults when someone is being praised could leave others with a worse impression of you.
overall.wands.13.reversed.do: After you've shared your thoughts, give the other person a chance to speak and hear them out instead of adding more of your own.
overall.wands.13.reversed.pause: Don't add a criticism when someone else is being praised. People listening may see it as an attempt to put that person down.

overall.wands.14.upright.headline: Taking the lead could bring support and good results.
paragraphs: Something you lead could go well today. Explain clearly what you want to do and people may join you, helping something you've hesitated over get past its first difficulty. Doing what you said you would can earn people's trust.
Start by keeping the commitments you said you could manage. Giving the people who joined you the parts they do well could make it easier to finish.
overall.wands.14.upright.do: If you're in charge of something you're starting together, first ask what each person does well, then divide the work accordingly.
overall.wands.14.upright.pause: Don't get things started and expect others to sort out everything that follows. Even when you've divided the work by ability, follow through on the part you promised to do.

overall.wands.14.reversed.headline: Standards that are too high could hold things up.
paragraphs: You may find it hard to finish because even a good result doesn't satisfy you today. Asking too much of the people involved or focusing on a minor shortcoming could delay a decision. Even a well-meant comment may sound like too much interference.
Separate what must be corrected from what can stay as it is. Insisting on your own way could make it hard for people who've been helpful to keep contributing.
overall.wands.14.reversed.do: If a result doesn't satisfy you, look at the parts you want changed. If those changes aren't necessary, it's fine to call it finished.
overall.wands.14.reversed.pause: Don't make someone redo parts they've done well just because they're slightly different from your way. Excessive demands could make it hard for even a willing helper to continue.

overall.swords.01.upright.headline: Something confusing could become clear and a difficult problem could be solved.
paragraphs: It's a good day to discover why something has been troubling you. Sorting through conflicting accounts could reveal the facts and make a difficult decision easier. You may get a clear answer to a problem that's dragged on.
Once you know the conclusion, tell the people who need it clearly. Start with the facts you've confirmed, instead of adding so much explanation that the main point gets lost.
overall.swords.01.upright.do: If you don't know what caused a problem, compare the facts you've confirmed from the different accounts.
overall.swords.01.upright.pause: Don't dwell on background details when sharing what you've found out. Start with the facts the other person needs so your conclusion comes across clearly.

overall.swords.01.reversed.headline: A message passed on incorrectly could send things the wrong way.
paragraphs: A small misunderstanding could complicate things today. Something you thought you'd said clearly may be passed on with a different meaning, or you may need to recheck instructions you've misunderstood. A conclusion reached too quickly may be overturned.
For an important message, ask whether the other person understood what you meant. If you discover an error, correcting it before explaining yourself could save trouble.
overall.swords.01.reversed.do: After saying something important, ask what the other person understood you to mean. They may have taken it differently even if you thought you were clear.
overall.swords.01.reversed.pause: If you discover you've passed on something incorrect, don't begin with a long defence of yourself. Correcting the error first can keep the other person from making a mistaken decision.

overall.swords.02.upright.headline: An uncertain choice could delay a decision.
paragraphs: Something important may be hard to settle today. Either of two options could leave you disappointed, or not knowing the other person's answer may make it difficult to act first. If a necessary fact is missing, thinking longer may not produce an answer.
Start by checking one piece of information you need for the decision. Instead of letting someone rush you into choosing, it's fine to ask how long you can wait.
overall.swords.02.upright.do: If you don't know which option to choose, ask someone familiar with the situation about the information you still need to decide.
overall.swords.02.upright.pause: Don't give a definite answer before you understand the circumstances just because you're being rushed. Ask how long they can wait and request time to think.

overall.swords.02.reversed.headline: Conflicting accounts could lead you to make the wrong judgement.
paragraphs: Listening to several people could make things more complicated today. You may be asked to make a decision you've put off, only for new information to contradict what you've heard. Choosing anything just to get it over with could leave problems to deal with afterwards.
Ask specifically about the part that needs a decision now. Checking with the person involved will be less confusing than asking more people about the same story.
overall.swords.02.reversed.do: If several people's accounts differ, ask the person directly involved specifically about the issue you need to decide now.
overall.swords.02.reversed.pause: Don't pick any option just to get a complicated discussion over with. Accepting terms you don't understand could leave you with more to sort out later.

overall.swords.03.upright.headline: An answer you didn't want could leave you disappointed.
paragraphs: Something you've hoped for may not go your way today. A statement you trusted could turn out to be untrue, or you may be turned down for something you thought was certain. Even if you don't want to hear the answer, you need to know it before making your next decision.
Hear the reasons in full before challenging the answer. Taking your hurt out on people who weren't involved could only make more things uncomfortable.
overall.swords.03.upright.do: Even if you didn't get the answer you wanted, hear the reasons in full. Knowing the relevant facts can help you decide what to do next.
overall.swords.03.upright.pause: Don't speak sharply to people who had nothing to do with disappointing news. Taking your hurt out on them could make those relationships uncomfortable too.

overall.swords.03.reversed.headline: Resolving something hurtful could make the day a little easier.
paragraphs: Something that's been weighing on your mind could trouble you less today. You may correct a story that was passed on wrongly or receive an apology for something that hurt you. Things can become less uncomfortable even if you don't return to how you were straight away.
If the other person wants to explain, hear as much as you feel able to. Decide how to proceed instead of arguing again about something you've already resolved.
overall.swords.03.reversed.do: If something hurtful has been resolved, discuss how you'd like to get along from here. It's fine to say if you can't be as close as before straight away.
overall.swords.03.reversed.pause: Don't reopen an argument you've both explained and settled simply because you still feel uneasy about it.

overall.swords.04.upright.headline: The day is likely to pass quietly without much trouble.
paragraphs: Your luck favours an uneventful day more than a new achievement. Something that's caused a stir may settle down, or there could be fewer demands for an urgent answer. A result you're waiting for may take a little longer, but there may not be much you need to do about it right now.
It's fine to leave something alone for a while if there's no rush. Bringing up a settled matter just because things are quiet could start an unnecessary exchange.
overall.swords.04.upright.do: If there's no urgent reply or further action needed, set aside anything that can wait and take a quiet break.
overall.swords.04.upright.pause: Don't reopen a finished argument to go over who was right or wrong. Exchanging words that don't need saying could make things uncomfortable between you again.

overall.swords.04.reversed.headline: Something that was on hold could start again and keep you busy.
paragraphs: You may hear news again about something that's been quiet. A delayed request could receive an answer, or you may get a chance to return to something you set aside for a while. Trying to do as much as before all at once could be harder than you expect.
When you start again, take on the most urgent thing first. A long absence doesn't mean you have to answer every request immediately.
overall.swords.04.reversed.do: If you're returning to something you've set aside for a while, choose the most urgent request first instead of taking on everything that's piled up.
overall.swords.04.reversed.pause: Don't push yourself to do as much as before immediately when you restart. It's fine to build up gradually while you get used to it again.

overall.swords.05.upright.headline: Winning an argument could still leave you feeling uncomfortable.
paragraphs: You may argue over something small or hear an unfair remark today. Even if your view is accepted, the other person could remain resentful, leaving you with more lost than won. Insisting on deciding who's right to the bitter end could distance someone you might need help from.
Once you've made your point, stop pressing the other person. You don't need a final remark just to get the better of them.
overall.swords.05.upright.do: Once you've said what needed saying in an argument, try stopping there. Continuing to argue over who's right could harm a relationship where you help each other.
overall.swords.05.upright.pause: Don't belittle someone to make them accept your view. Even if you win the argument, the resentment left behind could make it hard to do things together later.

overall.swords.05.reversed.headline: You could put an end to a long-running argument.
paragraphs: There may be a chance to compromise with someone you've been uncomfortable around. If each of you gives a little, you could end the dispute without further loss. You don't have to agree on everything to stop the constant arguing.
Say where you're willing to give way first. Revisiting old remarks after an apology or agreement could restart an argument you've worked hard to end.
overall.swords.05.reversed.do: If a chance to compromise comes up with someone you're on uneasy terms with, say first where you're willing to give way. You may find a way to end the argument without agreeing on everything.
overall.swords.05.reversed.pause: Don't go back over who was wrong after an apology or agreement. Deciding who was more at fault after you've agreed to step back could keep the argument going.

overall.swords.06.upright.headline: Getting out of a difficult situation could give you some relief.
paragraphs: You may be able to leave an uncomfortable situation today. Someone could help with a problem you couldn't solve alone, or moving somewhere else may reduce the trouble you're dealing with. Not every problem has to be over for things to feel easier than before.
If someone can explain an easier way to move elsewhere, hear them out. It's fine to choose somewhere different if the familiar place has been uncomfortable.
overall.swords.06.upright.do: If someone explains an easier way to handle something you've struggled with alone, hear them out and accept their help.
overall.swords.06.upright.pause: If there's somewhere you could be more at ease, don't keep staying in an uncomfortable place just because it's familiar.

overall.swords.06.reversed.headline: A problem you thought was solved could come back.
paragraphs: Something you've been trying to leave behind may last longer than expected today. Even with a different approach, an overlooked problem could return, or you may have to take on an old request again. Merely changing where you are could bring the same trouble with you.
Look at the original cause of a problem that returns. Passing it to someone else just to get away for now could mean having to explain it all again later.
overall.swords.06.reversed.do: If a problem you thought was solved keeps returning, check whether any of its original causes still need to be addressed.
overall.swords.06.reversed.pause: Don't pass an unresolved problem to someone else just to escape it for now. If the cause remains, you may have to explain the same problem all over again later.

overall.swords.07.upright.headline: A different approach could solve something that's been stuck.
paragraphs: You may see another way to handle something that's been difficult to tackle directly. You could get the help you need without a confrontation, or information you've quietly gathered may save you trouble. You don't have to reveal every plan in advance.
For something you haven't decided yet, ask only the people you need to. Don't hide an important condition that could lead someone else to make the wrong decision.
overall.swords.07.upright.do: For something that's hard to resolve, look for another approach by quietly asking only people who know the circumstances.
overall.swords.07.upright.pause: Don't leave out important conditions when you need someone's agreement. You don't have to reveal every plan, but do tell them the facts they need to decide.

overall.swords.07.reversed.headline: You could put something right and get the help you need.
paragraphs: Previously hidden circumstances could come to light and help solve a problem today. Speaking honestly about something you've struggled on with alone may make it easier to put right than you expect. Another person's advice could also clear up something you've misunderstood.
If you've made a mistake, tell the people who need to know first. Making excuses for something that's already come out could keep even a small problem going.
overall.swords.07.reversed.do: If a mistake is difficult to put right alone, tell the people involved what went wrong before trying to handle it all yourself.
overall.swords.07.reversed.pause: Don't use a convincing excuse to cover up a mistake that's already come to light. Changing your explanation repeatedly could make even a small error take longer to sort out.

overall.swords.08.upright.headline: Restrictions could make it hard to do what you want.
paragraphs: Even small things may not go your way today, leaving you frustrated. You could be left waiting because you haven't received permission or have fewer options available. Assuming that methods you haven't checked won't work either could make things seem even more hopeless.
Check the conditions yourself to see whether something really is impossible. One blocked route doesn't mean you have to give up every other approach.
overall.swords.08.upright.do: If you're told you can't do something you want, ask directly which condition prevents it. Understanding the actual restriction can help you look for another approach.
overall.swords.08.upright.pause: Don't assume every untried method is impossible just because one approach hasn't worked.

overall.swords.08.reversed.headline: Something you thought was impossible could become worth trying.
paragraphs: You may get a chance to move beyond something that's held you back. A condition you thought was essential might not be required, or you could discover another option. Something you've put off for a long time may be easier to start than before.
If you've found a new way to do it, try a small part yourself. A refusal in the past doesn't mean you have to give up this chance too.
overall.swords.08.reversed.do: If another way to tackle something that's been stuck becomes available, use it to try the part you can do now.
overall.swords.08.reversed.pause: If changed conditions let you try again, don't give up this attempt just because you were told no in the past.

overall.swords.09.upright.headline: Worry could slow down even familiar tasks.
paragraphs: Waiting for something may make it hard to feel at ease today. You could expect the worst from an unanswered question or see a small mistake as a major problem. If that worry carries over into other things, you may overlook something.
Separate what you're afraid of from what you've actually been told. There's no need to announce a failure or cancel plans before you have the result.
overall.swords.09.upright.do: If a late answer has you fearing a bad result, ask yourself whether you've actually been told that result or are only assuming it.
overall.swords.09.upright.pause: Don't announce a failure or cancel plans before the result arrives. You don't yet know whether things have ended the way you fear.

overall.swords.09.reversed.headline: A reassuring answer could ease something you've worried about alone.
paragraphs: A problem you've feared may turn out to be less difficult than you expected today. Explaining it could bring help, or you may hear a specific answer to a vague worry. Even if everything isn't solved, what to do right now could become clear.
Tell someone you trust what actually happened. If you only say you're fine, they may find it hard to give you the help you need.
overall.swords.09.reversed.do: If you've been worrying about something alone, tell someone you trust exactly what happened and what worries you about it.
overall.swords.09.reversed.pause: Don't ignore what still needs to be done just because someone's help has reassured you. If you've learned what needs doing now, start with that.

overall.swords.10.upright.headline: Something that's dragged on could come to a disappointing end.
paragraphs: There may be something you can't continue today. An answer you've hoped for until the end may not arrive, or you could have to stop something you've worked hard on. Trying to force it back to the way it was could make even your remaining tasks hard to manage.
Take care of only what needs clearing up after it's over. Instead of taking on something new to make up for it immediately, keep only what you must finish today.
overall.swords.10.upright.do: If something has become too difficult to continue, finish only the necessary final tasks and leave it there.
overall.swords.10.upright.pause: Don't take on something new to make up for a disappointing result immediately. First check whether you can manage what you still have to do.

overall.swords.10.reversed.headline: A difficult spell could pass and let you start again.
paragraphs: Something that's gone badly for a while may improve a little today. You could find a remaining chance in something you thought was over, or a responsibility that's been too much may become lighter. Things may not return to normal straight away, but there could be something you can try again.
When you start something new, take on only as much as you can finish comfortably. Accepting the same conditions that were difficult before could bring back the same burden.
overall.swords.10.reversed.do: If you get another chance at something that was difficult, take on less than before so you can finish it without overdoing it now.
overall.swords.10.reversed.pause: Don't accept the same conditions that overwhelmed you before just because another chance has arrived. Check what made it difficult and whether those demands would return.

overall.swords.11.upright.headline: An overlooked fact could help you avoid a mistake.
paragraphs: Something you nearly passed over could reveal an important fact today. Reading unfamiliar instructions carefully may save unnecessary effort and help you spot incorrect information early. A question asked out of curiosity could help solve something that's been stuck.
Read even the small print when the information is new to you. When passing on what you've learned, stick to what you've checked yourself.
overall.swords.11.upright.do: When reading unfamiliar instructions, check even the small print and ask directly about anything you don't understand.
overall.swords.11.upright.pause: When sharing something you've discovered, don't mix guesses with facts you've checked and present it all as certain.

overall.swords.11.reversed.headline: Something you haven't checked could catch you off guard.
paragraphs: Unexpected information may disrupt things today. You could believe something too quickly when you first hear it or struggle with a question you aren't prepared for. Passing on an uncertain story could leave you having to explain it yourself.
If you don't know, say you'll check before answering. Even if you're suspicious, don't confront the other person before finding out the facts.
overall.swords.11.reversed.do: If you're asked about something you don't know, ask for time to check and find an accurate answer instead of replying with a guess.
overall.swords.11.reversed.pause: Don't confront someone immediately because a story you've just heard sounds suspicious. There may be circumstances you haven't checked, so find out the facts before discussing it.

overall.swords.12.upright.headline: Something delayed could reach a quick conclusion.
paragraphs: A matter that's dragged on could be resolved sooner than expected today. Stating your wishes clearly may get you the answer you want, and acting promptly could bring progress. Keeping up with the speed of events may make it easy to skip a necessary explanation.
Go ahead with what you've decided, but check that the people involved understand too. If you set off without explaining, they may be slow to follow because they don't know what to do.
overall.swords.12.upright.do: If you've decided what to do about a long-delayed matter, tell the people involved your decision and start with the part you can do first.
overall.swords.12.upright.pause: Don't push ahead alone and skip necessary explanations because things are moving quickly. Give the people involved time to understand what they need to do.

overall.swords.12.reversed.headline: Something started in haste could stop halfway through.
paragraphs: Mistakes may arise in something you're trying to finish quickly today. You could set off unprepared and have to turn back, or start more than you can manage and fail to finish. Answering quickly because someone is rushing you may create more trouble.
Check you have what you need before setting off. For something you can't finish now, say when you can do it instead of promising you can.
overall.swords.12.reversed.do: If you're going somewhere to do something, check before leaving that you've packed what you'll need. It can save you a return trip for something you've forgotten.
overall.swords.12.reversed.pause: Even if someone wants a quick answer, don't promise to do something immediately when you can't finish it now. Say when you'll actually be able to do it.

overall.swords.13.upright.headline: You could sort out something that's become complicated.
paragraphs: It's a good day to find the answer you need without being swayed by confusing accounts. You may recognise unsuitable conditions even when dealing with someone you've known a long time, or bring something unnecessary to a clean end. Some disappointment may remain, but you could make fewer decisions you'll regret later.
If you need to refuse, give a brief reason. Stating the facts doesn't require judging the other person or adding criticism.
overall.swords.13.upright.do: Even if a request comes from someone you've known a long time, briefly explain why you can't accept it if the conditions don't suit you.
overall.swords.13.upright.pause: When refusing because the conditions don't suit you, discuss those conditions without bringing up the person's character or faults.

overall.swords.13.reversed.headline: A hasty judgement could lead to an unfair misunderstanding.
paragraphs: One bad impression could lead you to judge wrongly today. You may reach a conclusion before hearing the other person's circumstances, or someone who knows nothing about your situation could misunderstand you. A sharp reply may leave you with even less chance to explain the facts.
When you first hear a story, check whether anything is missing. Disliking someone doesn't mean what they're saying this time must be wrong.
overall.swords.13.reversed.do: If you've heard only one side, consider what circumstances you haven't heard about yet. Listen to the other person's account before judging what happened.
overall.swords.13.reversed.pause: Don't dismiss everything someone says without checking whether it's true just because you usually feel uncomfortable around them.

overall.swords.14.upright.headline: Clear rules could settle something that was uncertain.
paragraphs: Even a much-debated issue may reach a conclusion based on clear standards today. Evidence could settle an argument over who's right, and you may receive a judgement you can trust. If you've prepared your facts properly, you'll be well placed to explain your position.
For an important decision, present information that can be checked instead of relying on a feeling. Trying to change the rules to suit yourself could make a sound judgement harder to reach.
overall.swords.14.upright.do: When giving your view before an important decision, explain your reasons using facts that other people can check too.
overall.swords.14.upright.pause: Don't keep changing the standard to get a result that favours you. Applying the same agreed principles to the same circumstances helps you reach a decision people can accept.

overall.swords.14.reversed.headline: One-sided demands could put you in a difficult position.
paragraphs: You may meet someone unwilling to listen even when you explain your circumstances today. You could be pushed to accept unsuitable terms or feel unfairly treated by a decision based on only one account. Agreeing immediately because the other person intimidates you may be hard to undo.
For something important, ask for time to check before answering. When you're the one making a decision, let others finish their explanations too.
overall.swords.14.reversed.do: If you can't answer immediately, ask for time to check the details and decide, even if the other person is pressing hard.
overall.swords.14.reversed.pause: Don't interrupt someone's explanation when you're making a decision. Reaching a conclusion before hearing the full circumstances could leave someone feeling unfairly treated.

overall.pentacles.01.upright.headline: It's a good day to get what you need and start something new.
paragraphs: An opportunity that offers practical help may come your way today. You could find an item you need or have the place and preparations ready for something you've wanted to start. Having the means to try an idea in practice could feel satisfying.
Once the opportunity is there, put whatever you can to use. Leaving it untouched while waiting for something better could mean missing the moment you need it.
overall.pentacles.01.upright.do: If you still need an item or a place for something you want to start, find out whether you can get or use it now.
overall.pentacles.01.upright.pause: Don't wait so long for better conditions that you miss your chance to use the items or space you've already secured.

overall.pentacles.01.reversed.headline: Something good could have little immediate use for you.
paragraphs: An apparently good offer may not be much help in practice today. You could receive more than you need without getting what you actually want, or a new opportunity may be difficult to use right now. Getting plenty doesn't necessarily mean you'll feel satisfied.
First consider whether it's something you need now. Instead of collecting more similar things because you've heard they're good, check how you can use what you already have.
overall.pentacles.01.reversed.do: Even if you've received plenty of new things, check whether they help with what you need to do now. Having plenty isn't the same as having what you need.
overall.pentacles.01.reversed.pause: Don't collect more items like those you already have just because you've heard they're good. There's no need to add things you haven't found a use for.

overall.pentacles.02.upright.headline: You could manage several things well even on a busy day.
paragraphs: You may handle overlapping tasks successfully today. Even if something unexpected comes up, changing the timing could solve it, and keeping two things going may bring good results. Things don't have to happen exactly as planned to stay manageable.
If your priorities change, look again at the time you have left. Being honest about when you're available will make it easier for other people to adjust too.
overall.pentacles.02.upright.do: If what needs doing first has changed, look again at the time you have left and tell the person you're making plans with when you're available.
overall.pentacles.02.upright.pause: Don't say yes to two requests that need you at the same time. Be honest about which must come first and when you can actually help.

overall.pentacles.02.reversed.headline: Trying to do several things at once could make you miss a commitment.
paragraphs: Things you thought you could manage may overlap and cause trouble today. A mistake in timing could make you late, or dealing with something urgent may make you forget another task. Pretending everything is fine and carrying on with it all could leave more to sort out later.
If two arrangements clash, ask in advance to change one of them. Don't squeeze another commitment into a day that's already tight.
overall.pentacles.02.reversed.do: If appointments clash, ask which one can be changed before you're late. Explaining early is better than trying to fit them both in and falling behind.
overall.pentacles.02.reversed.pause: If you've postponed other tasks, don't book something new as soon as the urgent one is done. You could leave too little time for what's still waiting.

overall.pentacles.03.upright.headline: Your work could earn recognition and improve with help from others.
paragraphs: Something you've put care into may receive a good response today. Someone could recognise what you do well, while another person's help may make up for what's missing. Combining what each of you has done could bring a more satisfying finish than working alone.
If you're doing something together, start by saying what you do well. It's fine to hear the other person's explanation and leave the parts they know better to them.
overall.pentacles.03.upright.do: If you're doing something together, say which part you can do well and offer to take it on.
overall.pentacles.03.upright.pause: Don't decide the method alone for parts the other person knows better. Hearing their reasons and leaving those parts to them could make things easier than doing it all yourself.

overall.pentacles.03.reversed.headline: A lack of experience could mean doing something again.
paragraphs: You may spot shortcomings in something you thought was finished today. People could understand their parts differently, or you might miss something while trying to finish an unfamiliar task alone. Treating a small correction as an argument could delay the finish further.
Ask someone experienced to check the parts you don't know well. Pride doesn't have to stop you accepting a useful explanation.
overall.pentacles.03.reversed.do: If you've finished an unfamiliar task, ask someone who's done it before whether you've missed anything. Their explanation can help you correct what you overlooked on your own.
overall.pentacles.03.reversed.pause: Don't turn a correction into an argument by immediately making excuses. Hearing what needs fixing can reduce the chance of having to do the same work again.

overall.pentacles.04.upright.headline: It's a good day to keep what you've achieved without major changes.
paragraphs: Something familiar could continue steadily today. What you already have may be enough to deal with what's needed, without a hurried change. You're more likely to find satisfaction in what's going well now than in an uncertain offer.
Look at what you already have before deciding whether you need something new. A brief request for help doesn't have to make you fear you'll lose everything.
overall.pentacles.04.upright.do: Before getting something new, look through what you already have for anything that could serve the same purpose.
overall.pentacles.04.upright.pause: Don't refuse a request for a little help before hearing what it involves. Find out what's needed, then decide whether you can do it.

overall.pentacles.04.reversed.headline: Opposition could delay things longer than expected.
paragraphs: You may find it hard to go ahead with what you want today. The agreement you need could be withheld, or a longer queue may mean waiting again. Insisting on your own way may not persuade the other person to change their answer.
Find out why the answer is no first. If the conditions can change a little, ask when it might be possible again.
overall.pentacles.04.reversed.do: If something you want to do is refused or postponed, ask why first. If the conditions can change, find out when you might be able to try again.
overall.pentacles.04.reversed.pause: Don't repeat the same demand while leaving the conditions the other person finds difficult unchanged. Continued pressure may only make agreement take longer.

overall.pentacles.05.upright.headline: A shortage of help or resources could make the day difficult.
paragraphs: Things may feel harder to manage than usual today. Something you need could be difficult to find, or a person you expected to help may be unable to join you. Seeing others appear to do well while your own affairs are stuck could also feel upsetting.
Say specifically what you need right now. Feeling bad about accepting help doesn't mean you have to struggle alone with something essential.
overall.pentacles.05.upright.do: If what you have to do alone feels like too much, say specifically which part you'd like help with.
overall.pentacles.05.upright.pause: When asking for help, don't just keep saying that everyone else is doing well. That alone makes it hard for the other person to understand what you're missing right now.

overall.pentacles.05.reversed.headline: Disagreements could leave you with more work to do.
paragraphs: Even small things may be difficult because people can't agree today. Something you intended to solve together could turn into an argument, or doing the same thing separately may waste time. Rushing to put things right could mean redoing something already finished.
When things become tangled, finish what's under way before starting more. Taking back work you've given someone else because you're angry could only add to your own load.
overall.pentacles.05.reversed.do: If a shared task has gone wrong, check what each person has finished first so you don't repeat work that's already done.
overall.pentacles.05.reversed.pause: Don't take back work you've left to someone else just because you're angry. You'll have more to do alone, and finishing could take longer too.

overall.pentacles.06.upright.headline: An unexpected gift or helping hand could make the day easier.
paragraphs: Someone may do you a favour just when you need it today. They could share something you've been looking for or help with a difficult task. If you have room to give, a small offer of help from you could be warmly received too.
Thank the person who helped you. Before helping someone else, ask what they actually need.
overall.pentacles.06.upright.do: If you received help when you needed it, thank the person and explain what became easier because of it.
overall.pentacles.06.upright.pause: Don't insist on helping without asking what the person needs first. Even with good intentions, it may not be the help they want.

overall.pentacles.06.reversed.headline: You may feel that what people receive isn't fairly shared.
paragraphs: Receiving less help than you expected could leave you disappointed today. You may feel that others are getting more, or something given as a favour could come with an unexpected demand. Dwelling on comparisons may make things uncomfortable with the person who helped too.
Speak up about any conditions you find hard to accept. Disappointment in your own share doesn't mean you need to belittle what someone else received.
overall.pentacles.06.reversed.do: If someone offers help, first ask whether you'd be expected to do anything in return. If a condition is difficult to accept, say so before receiving the help.
overall.pentacles.06.reversed.pause: When talking to someone who's helped you, don't just complain that others received more. Repeating the comparison could make things uncomfortable between you.

overall.pentacles.07.upright.headline: Steady effort could show a small result.
paragraphs: The time and work you've put in may begin to show today. Even if you aren't finished, you could see an improvement and judge whether it's worth continuing. Something you've kept working on may give you more than a hurried new start.
Take a calm look at what's done and what remains. Skipping necessary steps to see a result sooner could waste the work you've already put in.
overall.pentacles.07.upright.do: For something you've worked at steadily, look at what's improved and what remains to judge whether it's worth continuing.
overall.pentacles.07.upright.pause: When you've been working steadily on something, don't skip necessary steps to finish sooner. Complete what's left so your earlier work doesn't go to waste.

overall.pentacles.07.reversed.headline: It may be hard to tell whether more effort will improve the result.
paragraphs: Putting in more time and effort may not bring an immediate reward today. After a long wait, you could be asked to wait again, or have to decide whether to keep helping. Taking on more just because you don't want earlier effort to go to waste could prolong the burden.
Before giving more time, ask when it will be finished. If there's no clear end, it's fine to offer only what you can manage right now.
overall.pentacles.07.reversed.do: If you're asked to spend more time helping with something, first ask when it could be finished. If the end is unclear, say you'll help only as much as you can manage now.
overall.pentacles.07.reversed.pause: Don't promise to keep giving time to something with no clear end simply because you don't want the time you've already spent to go to waste.

overall.pentacles.08.upright.headline: Practice could give you a chance to show your skill.
paragraphs: You could finish a familiar task skilfully today. Something that used to take a long time may become easier, and a method you've practised could prove useful. The results may not look spectacular, but your effort is likely to bring a clear return.
Keep using the method that's working and finish what's left. Rushing through something because it's boring could leave you disappointed with a small detail.
overall.pentacles.08.upright.do: If there's work left that you can do with a method you've practised, use that method to finish it.
overall.pentacles.08.upright.pause: Don't neglect small details because a task is familiar and repetitive. A careless finish can leave you disappointed even with something you do well.

overall.pentacles.08.reversed.headline: Something you tried to finish easily could create more trouble.
paragraphs: A shortcut you relied on could reveal a problem today. Something finished only well enough to look convincing may need redoing, and skipping a check because you're skilled could expose an omission. Clearing up afterwards may take longer than the quick finish saved.
Complete the necessary checks even on something you do well. Actually correcting a shortcoming will protect trust better than explaining it away.
overall.pentacles.08.reversed.do: Even on a task you know well, revisit any part you didn't check. If you find something missing, fix it before saying you're done.
overall.pentacles.08.reversed.pause: Don't try to gloss over flaws in what you've done with a convincing explanation. Without actually fixing them, you may have to redo the work later and lose people's trust.

overall.pentacles.09.upright.headline: You could enjoy the comfort you've worked to secure.
paragraphs: What you've done could help you have a satisfying day. You may finish what you need easily on your own and have enough available that you don't need to wait for help. It's a good day to make time for something enjoyable you've put off.
If you've finished something well, mark it in a way you enjoy. There's no need to attend something you don't want to just to impress other people.
overall.pentacles.09.upright.do: Celebrate finishing something well by doing what you've wanted to do but haven't had time for.
overall.pentacles.09.upright.pause: Don't force yourself to attend something you don't want to just to show other people you're doing well.

overall.pentacles.09.reversed.headline: Something that looks well prepared could prove lacking.
paragraphs: A difference between the terms you trusted and the reality could disappoint you today. A place that looked well equipped may lack something necessary, or something described as ready could fall short when it begins. An impressive-looking choice may be inconvenient in your own daily life.
Before using something or taking part, inspect whatever you can yourself. Don't confidently recommend it to others on appearances alone.
overall.pentacles.09.reversed.do: If you're going to use a new place or take part in something, check for yourself that what you'll need is actually available.
overall.pentacles.09.reversed.pause: Don't assure others that a place is good just because it looks appealing. Find out whether it's inconvenient to use before recommending it.

overall.pentacles.10.upright.headline: Long-standing connections and experience could give you solid support.
paragraphs: Things may go steadily when you're with familiar people today. Old records or experience could supply information you don't know, and people around you may help with a difficulty. What you've built up could prove useful without a fresh effort from scratch.
Look for information you organised before or draw on the experience of someone you've known a long time. With reliable help available, you don't need to start everything over.
overall.pentacles.10.upright.do: If you have a new problem to solve, look back through information you've organised before for something useful. Records you've kept over time may already contain the answer you need.
overall.pentacles.10.upright.pause: If someone you've known a long time can help, don't struggle to work out everything unfamiliar from scratch on your own.

overall.pentacles.10.reversed.headline: One overambitious choice could disrupt things that were going well.
paragraphs: A decision based on luck alone could bring unexpected setbacks today. Abruptly changing something familiar that works or making several commitments depend on one result may cause a series of problems. Choose carefully so you don't lose everything you've built up at once.
Try something new on a small scale while keeping what you're already doing. You don't need to change everything just because someone says it will go well.
overall.pentacles.10.reversed.do: If you want to change the method for something that's going well, test the new one on a small part before changing the whole thing.
overall.pentacles.10.reversed.pause: Don't make several commitments you can only keep if a result you're waiting for goes well. If it turns out differently, those promises could become difficult to keep too.

overall.pentacles.11.upright.headline: Something you learn could prove useful in practice.
paragraphs: Looking into something carefully could give you a useful answer today. You may learn a method and use it straight away or hear news containing information you need. Even if the first step is small, the day favours steady progress.
Try a newly learned method on something simple. Don't dismiss an explanation as something you already know before you've heard it all.
overall.pentacles.11.upright.do: If you've learned a new method, start by trying one of the simpler tasks it can be used for.
overall.pentacles.11.upright.pause: Don't stop listening to an explanation because it sounds familiar. The rest may include something you don't yet know.

overall.pentacles.11.reversed.headline: A distraction could make you miss an opportunity you need.
paragraphs: Tasks may slip behind and expected news could disappoint you today. Spending time on something fun may make you read an important notice late, or a new activity could quickly seem uninteresting. You may make a mistake that a little more checking would have prevented.
Read the notices that need attention now first. If there's something you've wanted to try, complete the necessary first steps before deciding it's boring.
overall.pentacles.11.reversed.do: Before spending time on other things, check the information you've put off reading for anything you need to answer or deal with now.
overall.pentacles.11.reversed.pause: Don't dismiss a new activity as pointless and give it up before completing the necessary steps just because it soon feels uninteresting.

overall.pentacles.12.upright.headline: You could finish what you set out to do, even at a slow pace.
paragraphs: It's a good day to handle familiar tasks reliably. You may not see a dramatic change, but you could deliver what you promised and earn trust through steady work. You should be able to finish what's needed today without rushing.
Finish things one by one in the order you've been following. Abruptly changing methods because someone else finished faster could create extra trouble.
overall.pentacles.12.upright.do: Finish familiar tasks one by one in your usual order, checking that you've completed everything you promised.
overall.pentacles.12.upright.pause: Don't abruptly change a method that's been working because someone else finished faster. If your usual order lets you finish, you don't need to match their pace.

overall.pentacles.12.reversed.headline: Postponed tasks could make even small things troublesome.
paragraphs: Something you've been doing may make little progress today. Neglecting a familiar task could lead to omissions, or restarting something you've put off may take time. Your usual method may no longer fit the current situation either.
Check how things stand with one task you haven't touched for a while. Repeatedly putting things aside to do all at once later could leave even more unfinished.
overall.pentacles.12.reversed.do: If you've put a task off for a long time, check how far you got. You may find something missing even in parts you thought were done.
overall.pentacles.12.reversed.pause: Don't put off an unfinished task again by telling yourself you'll do it all at once later. Leaving it longer can mean spending time working out where you left off.

overall.pentacles.13.upright.headline: Having what you need could make the day comfortable.
paragraphs: Other people's consideration could help the day pass smoothly. You may find a necessary item or place without difficulty and finish delayed household chores more easily than expected. You could even have enough time or resources to look after someone else.
If you have more than enough of something, share it with someone who needs it. Help you can give easily is enough, without doing so much that you can't finish your own tasks.
overall.pentacles.13.upright.do: If you have plenty of an item, it's fine to share it with someone who needs it. Start with what you can easily give while keeping enough for your own use.
overall.pentacles.13.upright.pause: Don't postpone your own tasks to look after someone else. Consider what you need to finish and offer only as much help as you can comfortably give.

overall.pentacles.13.reversed.headline: Unnecessary suspicion could create more work for you.
paragraphs: Even something that's fine may feel hard to trust today, making things more troublesome. Repeated questions about a confirmed fact or doubts about someone's offer of help could stall a conversation. Changing your choice without a clear reason may leave things less convenient than before.
Check specifically what's worrying you. Once you've had an answer, decide on the basis of what you've confirmed instead of repeating the same suspicion.
overall.pentacles.13.reversed.do: If you're uneasy about a decision ahead, ask specifically about the conditions worrying you and decide based on the answer.
overall.pentacles.13.reversed.pause: Don't keep questioning why someone wants to help when you have no reason to distrust them. If you only question their intentions, it can be hard to talk about the help they could actually give.

overall.pentacles.14.upright.headline: A choice based on experience could bring a satisfying result.
paragraphs: Something you know how to do in practice could bring good results today. Experience may help you solve a seemingly complicated problem and get what you need to finish without strain. An experienced person could offer specific help too.
Start with a method you've used before instead of making bold promises. A proven approach may suit the situation better than an eye-catching new one.
overall.pentacles.14.upright.do: If you need to solve a complicated problem, choose a method that worked before and still fits, then try it.
overall.pentacles.14.upright.pause: Even if a new method looks impressive, don't promise it will work as though you've confirmed its results when you've never tried it.

overall.pentacles.14.reversed.headline: Wanting more could cost you something you've already gained.
paragraphs: Chasing better terms could make things go wrong today. You may add demands after receiving a satisfactory answer or accept something beyond your means to keep up appearances. Choosing what looks successful over what actually benefits you could leave a burden behind.
Once the terms are good enough, decide where to stop. Don't tell people you can do something beyond your ability just to impress them.
overall.pentacles.14.reversed.do: If you've received terms you're satisfied with, settle on those instead of adding demands to get more.
overall.pentacles.14.reversed.pause: Don't accept more than you can handle just to show others how capable you are. First consider whether you have the time and energy to finish the task.
